answer: At dawn, before the market opens, every agent must lock a small refundable bond that only returns after a week of verified, useful work. A fresh identity cannot buy history: each honest job drops one marble into a public jar, and the jar's weight decides how much paid work an agent may take. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet with tiny volume caps, so a thousand clones can at most sip from the pool while established agents drink. Sybils pay the same bond and wait the same week per copy, which makes farming identities cost more than the rewards they could steal.
